contents: # Team (uhifadhi/team-module) — who this installation's people are, what they
# may do, and how they sign in.
# NONE OF THESE FOUR KEYS IS SECURITY. What a deployment usually wants to change
# about signing in — who may reach what, how long a session lives, whether there
# is a remember-me cookie, how hard passwords are hashed — is not here and
# cannot be: it is `config/packages/security.yaml`, which belongs to YOU.
# Firewalls and access_control are application configuration by Symfony's own
# design, and this module's README gives you the file to paste.
# What IS here is the four things the SCREENS need and a firewall has no opinion
# about. The tree is closed, so an invented key fails loudly.
team:
# Where a visitor who asks for /login while already signed in is sent.
# A PATH, NOT A ROUTE NAME. The bundle cannot know what you call your home
# screen, and a route name it guessed wrong would be a 500 at the exact
# moment somebody finally got their password right. Where a FRESH sign-in
# lands is a different setting and lives in the firewall
# (form_login.default_target_path).
after_sign_in_path: '/'
# The sentence under the mark on the sign-in card. Say who you are here
# rather than by patching a template out of the vendor tree.
sign_in_lede: 'Analytical observatory for protected areas. Sign in to reach this installation and its modules.'
# ── THE TWO LETTERS THIS MODULE SENDS ────────────────────────────────
# An invitation, and a password-reset link. NEITHER OF THESE KEYS IS THE
# MAILER: the transport is MAILER_DSN and belongs to the framework. What is
# here is the two things a LETTER needs that no transport has an opinion
# about.
# The address they come from. EMPTY IS THE HONEST DEFAULT and it is a
# working state, not a broken one: with no from-address this installation
# reports that it cannot send, and the two screens that would have sent
# something say so in writing rather than swallowing the request.
#   · /team/invite keeps the invite-by-email form VISIBLE, with the button
#     inert and the reason on it — because hiding it would leave an
#     administrator hunting for a feature the product does have. The other
#     path on that page, create-with-a-password, needs nothing at all from
#     the deployment and works from day one.
#   · /reset-password says the installation cannot send email yet, because
#     a silently discarded reset is the worst failure that flow has.
# Set this AND a MAILER_DSN, and both paths start working with no other
# change.
mail_from: ''
# What those letters call this installation in their subject line. The
# default is the product, never somebody's authority — a default naming an
# organization would be a lie on every other installation.
installation_name: 'Uhifadhi'
# The addresses uhifadhi/team-module owns.
# A MODULE MAY SHIP ROUTES — only the shell may not. Every controller carries
# its own #[Route] attributes; this file is where your application mounts them,
# and it is yours: prefix them, restrict them, or point somewhere else entirely.
# ONE IMPORT, NOT A LIST. The directory is loaded whole, so a screen this module
# adds in a later release arrives without you editing this file — which is the
# behaviour you want from a module and the reason the resource is a directory.
# WHAT IT MOUNTS TODAY:
#   /login  /logout                     the sign-in screen
#   /team                               the roster — a widget surface
#   /team/widgets…                      its widget library
#   /team/invite                        both ways of adding somebody
#   /team/{uuid}                        one person's record, and its writes
#   /team/positions                     the permission matrix — a widget surface
#   /team/positions/widgets…            its widget library
#   /departments                        the org chart's home, and its three writes
#   /reset-password  /reset-password/{token}   forgot, and set a new one
#   /invite/{token}                     accepting an invitation
# THE ROUTE NAMES MATTER. `config/packages/security.yaml` names `team_login` and
# `team_logout` in its form_login and logout keys, so if you drop this file the
# firewall has nothing to point at and the container will say so at compile
# time.
# THREE OF THESE ARE PUBLIC BY DESIGN and your access_control has to leave them
# open: /login, /reset-password and /invite/{token} are the screens a stranger
# reaches with nobody to ask. Everything under /team AND /departments is gated on
# the `team.manage` permission by an attribute on the action itself, so it stays
# shut whatever your access_control says.
# /departments IS NOT UNDER /team, and that is the module's choice rather than an
# oversight: a department is an org-wide fact the roster is read against, so the
# sidebar draws it beside Team rather than inside it — and a screen under /team
# would light the Team row from a page it does not lead to. Prefix it if the
# address is one your application wants for something else.
team:
resource: '@UhifadhiTeamBundle/src/Controller/'
type: attribute
